To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

higher intraindividual trial-by-trial reaction time variability in a perceptuo-motor task is related to increased dedifferentiation of episodic memory and (episodic) working memory functions in older adulthood.
higher intraindividual trial-by-trial variability is related to more memory forgetting in older age, which may be explained by a dedifferentiation between episodic memory and executive functions.
higher intraindividual RT variability is associated with dedifferentiated and impaired memory functions in old adults.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the within-person variability of cognitive functions is associated with dedifferentiation and memory performance.
the question of how intraindividual trial-by-trial performance variability in a speeded task is related to forgetting and dedifferentation of memory functions in old-age.
the role of RT variability in age-related changes in memory functions and the underlying neurobiological mechanisms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
higher RT variability is associated with a more dedifferentiated memory system, which may be related to impaired DA modulation in older adults.
higher intraindividual trial to trial variability in RT is associated with more episodic memory forgetting, and with more dedifferentiation of working and episodic memory.
higher RT variability is associated with less efficient consolidation processes in episodic memory and dedifferentiated cognitive functions in old adults.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
higher intraindividual RT variability is associated with dedifferentiation of episodic memory and other cognitive functions, as well as with increased forgetting in older adults.
higher RT variability in old age is associated with more dedifferentiated memory and working memory, which is related to more memory forgetting over a 1 week retention interval.
higher within-person trial-by-trial RT variability is related to more episodic memory forgetting and dedifferentiations in old age.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the degree of intraindividual trial-by-trial RT variability may be a useful index to predict individual differences in memory functions and their dedifferentiation in older adults.
the degree of trial-to-trial variability may be a useful indicator of individual differences in memory consolidation and cognitive dedifferentiation.

intraindividual trial-by-trial variability in perceptual speed is associated with memory performance and dedifferentiation in older adults, suggesting a role of dopamine in memory consolidation and cognitive dedifferentiation.
